question.prompt:
Consider the statements:

\((1)\) \(p\) and \(q\) are both true
 \((2)\) \(p\) is true and \(q\) is false
 \((3)\) \(p\) is false and \(q\) is true
 \((4)\) \(p\) is false and \(q\) is false.

How many of these imply the negation of the statement “\(p\) and \(q\) are both true”?

solutions.explanation:
The negation of both statements being true says that at least one of \(p\) and \(q\) is false.

Statement \((1)\) makes both true, so it does not imply the negation. Statement \((2)\) makes \(q\) false, statement \((3)\) makes \(p\) false, and statement \((4)\) makes both false. Thus each of \((2)\), \((3)\), and \((4)\) implies the negation.

These are all four listed cases, and exactly \(\boxed{3}\) qualify, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Identify when both are not true
